The query finds people who were authors on papers published 2019-2020 which were cited by refereed Harvard first-author papers in 2020, but who did not have a Harvard affiliation — potential colloquium speakers
natural_language: find potential colloquium speakers: authors whose work was cited by recent Harvard astronomy papers but who are not at Harvard

scenario: Historical example: searching for papers about globular clusters in the Andromeda Nebula (M31), used as input to the useful operator to show the Paper Network visualization

scenario: Find papers similar to a specific NED team abstract — the similar operator takes the abstract text, combines all abstracts into a single document, and ranks all ADS abstracts by text similarity

scenario: ScienceWriterX is writing about optical spectrographs and knows D. Fabricant's work — this finds his relevant papers

scenario: ScienceWriterX refines the similar query by excluding MMT papers and truncating to top 200 recent results — shows main projects and the importance of SPIE Conference Series

scenario: HistorianX is interested in the most influential work on stars and starts with Johnson & Morgan 1953, the fundamental paper for MK spectral classification and UBV photometry. Selecting 200 similar papers nearly uniformly samples 75 years of astronomical publications

scenario: Three levels deep: find the most cited papers among the 200 most similar to Johnson & Morgan 1953. Shows important research directions in classical stellar astronomy: narrow band photometry, Hipparcos, open clusters, model atmospheres, infrared photometry

scenario: Simple similar query on a topic — finds papers textually similar to weak lensing literature

scenario: Top 200 weak lensing papers sorted by relevance score rather than default sort

scenario: Temporal disjoint: find 2020 papers that are similar to 2019 weak lensing work. Forces the inner and outer results to be from different years, avoiding overlap

scenario: Current awareness: find very recent publications similar to those listed in the SETI bibliographic group — useful for maintainers of the SETI bibliography

scenario: Query the 'hive mind' model about Ultra Diffuse Galaxies — trending among readers of Chilingarian's references, filtered for UDG content
